title: The Problem with Buy Now Pay Later
summary: Creator examines Klarna's DoorDash partnership and argues BNPL's lack of regulation and fee structure specifically targets financially stretched shoppers.

assertions.quote: Both Afterpay and CLA proudly claim to boost average transaction sizes by 18 to 41% respectively.
people who use buy now pay later tend to be younger and without wellestablished credit and tend to shop in zip codes with fewer college
consumers don't have any real regulatory protection or dispute resolution options

verdicts.note: KC Fed: standardized dispute/refund protections were extended to BNPL only via a 2024 CFPB interpretive rule, not automatically the way they apply to credit cards, and the CFPB has since signaled plans to revoke that rule.

CFPB: Regulation Z requires credit-card issuers to provide billing-dispute and error-resolution rights, including the right to withhold payment during a dispute, but 'most BNPL lenders surveyed are currently not following Regulation Z's credit dispute resolution provisions.'

assertions.quote: buy now pay later is only going to encourage you to buy more than what you need
if any one of those payments are missed, a fee of up to $7 is charged to your already strained account

verdicts.note: Fed SHED: 64% of late payers (17% of all users) said they were charged extra for being late, and 11% of all users had a payment trigger a bank overdraft/NSF fee.

CFPB: three of five surveyed lenders charge late fees for missed payments (a flat fee or percentage of the missed installment), and unpaid loans are commonly referred to third-party debt collectors after reaching charged-off status -- consistent with a missed payment cascading into fees and then collections on an otherwise interest-free loan.

assertions.quote: it can also financially help constrain shoppers from resorting to highinterest credit cards
